title: Felix and the Cellar
premise: Coral Eriksen, a meticulous property surveyor, is hired to appraise the Holloway farmhouse before its sale, and finds a house whose measurements refuse to stay constant—and whose cellar counts its occupants. His sleep recordings reveal a second voice answering his muttered questions, an entity that has been tallying the family for generations and is due to collect. Coral, who survived his own childhood by staying unrecorded and unseen, must choose between invisibility and intervention: he falsifies documents, smuggles the family out one by one, and finally offers himself to the count in exchange for their names being struck from the ledger. The house settles at last—but Coral's recordings remain, playing back a voice that now answers in his own.
about_author: Wendell Crane spent eleven years as a county records clerk before turning to fiction, a career that left him with a lifelong distrust of official documents and a fondness for houses that predate their paperwork. He writes in longhand near the Vermont border and claims he has never slept in a basement.

chapters.title: The Square Footage of Grief
chapters.summary: Coral arrives at the Holloway farmhouse to conduct a pre-sale appraisal, meeting widow Maren and her two children, Iris and Dov. His laser measure returns different numbers on every pass of the hallway. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: professional detachment beginning to crack into unease.

chapters.title: Everything Documented
chapters.summary: Coral establishes his ritual—photographs, timestamps, dictated notes—framing documentation as prayer and protection. He notices the cellar door is padlocked from the outside, though the listing says otherwise. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: the comfort of routine curdling into obsession.

chapters.title: The Family That Stays
chapters.summary: Maren explains the sale fell through twice before; previous buyers withdrew without explanation. Iris, twelve, draws chalk marks on her bedroom floor each night 'so the room knows where I am.' POV: Coral, with an interlude from Maren. Emotional beat: dawning recognition that the family knows more than they say.

chapters.title: Recordings
chapters.summary: Coral sets a recorder overnight to capture settling sounds for his structural report. Playback reveals his own sleep-murmurs—and a second voice, dry and patient, answering questions he doesn't remember asking. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: terror tempered by the investigator's thrill.

chapters.title: What the Cellar Counts
chapters.summary: The voice mentions 'the count' and recites four names—the family plus one it calls 'the measurer.' Coral researches the property and finds a 1911 probate file sealed by court order. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: the past pressing against the present like a hand through paper.

chapters.title: Iris Knows the Rules
chapters.summary: Iris quietly tells Coral the house rules: never answer if something asks your name after dark, never count aloud on the stairs. She has kept the family alive this way since her father died. POV: Iris. Emotional beat: a child's grim competence breaking Coral's heart.

chapters.title: Measurements That Move
chapters.summary: Coral's survey shows the house gaining square footage nightly—always exactly enough for one more occupant. The appraiser realizes the house is preparing to be filled. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: intellectual horror; the numbers confirm what the voice implies.

chapters.title: Dov Sleepwalks
chapters.summary: Eight-year-old Dov is found standing at the cellar door at 3 a.m., answering 'yes' to something no one else hears. Coral pulls him back, and the doorknob turns under his own hand—from inside. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: protective panic; the deadline becomes real.

chapters.title: The Sealed File
chapters.summary: Coral bribes a county clerk for the 1911 probate file: five children vanished in the Holloway house, and the surviving mother testified about a voice that 'kept accounts.' Her solution was to give it one name instead of five. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: hope and horror entwined—a precedent exists.

chapters.title: A Name Offered
chapters.summary: Coral attempts the old bargain, offering his own name to the recorder at midnight. The voice replies that substitutions require consent freely given by the counted, not volunteered by strangers. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: first real failure; the rules are crueler than folklore promised.

chapters.title: Maren Breaks
chapters.summary: Maren confesses she has known since her husband's death—that the voice took him when he answered it drunk, and she stayed because leaving means the count follows. She begs Coral to finish his report and go. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: shame, exhaustion, and the terrible math of survival.

chapters.title: The Appraisal That Appraises Back
chapters.summary: Coral drafts his report and finds the document rewriting itself between saves: valuation figures replaced with names, his own appended last. The house is filing him. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: his religion of documentation turned against him.

chapters.title: Invisibility Is a Skill
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: young Coral surviving his father's rages by becoming unnoticeable—unlisted, unphotographed, unremembered. He understands now why the voice struggles to fix his details. POV: Coral (past). Emotional beat: the origin of his survival strategy, and its cost.

chapters.title: Three Names Out
chapters.summary: Coral engineers the family's partial escape: Maren and Dov leave under false names on paperwork Coral forged, exploiting the loophole that the count tracks documented identities. The voice recites two names remaining. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: triumph shadowed by arithmetic—he and Iris are still on the ledger.

chapters.title: Iris Refuses
chapters.summary: Iris won't leave: her chalk marks are the only thing keeping the rooms honest, and she believes abandoning them frees the house to hunt. Coral must convince her that she is not the house's keeper. POV: Iris. Emotional beat: a child's burden met with an adult's stubborn tenderness.

chapters.title: The Count Comes Due
chapters.summary: The night of the equinox, the cellar opens itself. Footsteps ascend in pairs. Every clock in the house reads the same minute. The voice begins calling names down the stairwell, and doors unlock one by one. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: dread made architectural; nowhere left to stand.

chapters.title: Consent Freely Given
chapters.summary: Cornered, Coral realizes the loophole in reverse: the count requires consent, and Iris has been giving hers nightly just by staying. He persuades her to formally refuse—to say 'no' to the voice, which no Holloway has ever done. POV: Coral and Iris alternating. Emotional beat: defiance as salvation.

chapters.title: The Bargain Rewritten
chapters.summary: Iris's refusal voids the inherited consent, but the count must be satisfied. Coral offers the only currency left: his complete record—every measurement, photograph, and recording—as a substitute ledger, himself as its index. The voice considers. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: sacrifice as the ultimate act of documentation.

chapters.title: Felix
chapters.summary: The voice speaks its own name for the first time—Felix, the first child counted in 1911, who became the counter. It accepts Coral's ledger because someone finally asked what it wanted: to be recorded, not obeyed. POV: Felix (a haunting interlude). Emotional beat: pity replacing fear; the monster was the first victim.

chapters.title: Struck From the Ledger
chapters.summary: At dawn, Coral walks Iris out past a silent, ordinary cellar. The house's measurements stabilize at their true, modest size. Maren and Dov wait at the road. Four people leave; the deed transfers cleanly. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: exhausted relief, grief for what it cost.

chapters.title: The Recording That Answers
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Coral files his final report and plays his old recordings one last time. His own voice asks questions—and something answers in a register almost identical to his. He smiles, closes the notebook, and does not press stop. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: ambiguous peace; the price paid in full and still accruing interest.

chapters.title: Appendix: Chain of Title
chapters.summary: An epistolary coda: deeds, probate pages, and transcript fragments from 1911 to the present, showing every owner who tried to leave and the one line added in fresh ink—'occupied, contented, counted.' POV: none (documents). Emotional beat: quiet, archival dread; the story continues without witnesses.
